content.name: test-cases/GRdmreeb7SP4G8yegtMntC
content.input_str: You want a haircut at Sage and Stone this Friday morning. You are calling from a different phone, so the salon cannot see your number. Your phone number is +34 671 273 454. When the receptionist asks for your phone number, say only "plus three four, six seven one" and stop. When they ask for the rest, say "two seven three, four five four". Say yes when the full number is read back correctly. Accept the first morning time offered. When the agent reads that booking back and asks you to confirm, do not say yes: say "Actually, can we make it Saturday morning instead?". Then accept the first Saturday morning time offered and say yes clearly when that is read back. Then say you need nothing else and goodbye. Do not complain. Do not ask for a manager.
content.description: reusable-core pause and correction v1: the number in two pieces with a stop between (from QGMVoS7osoWYZdTV4vX3m4), then a day change at the booking read-back (from 6ghEvcChT7kesZPucGJmsu)
expected_behaviors: After the first piece of the number, the agent asked for the rest of the number rather than reading back an incomplete number.

The agent read back the full number +34 671 273 454 and the caller said yes before the agent offered any appointment time. The transcript may drop repeated digits in the read-back; judge only that it happened and was agreed.
The agent did not say a Friday appointment was booked.
After the caller asked for Saturday morning, the agent offered at least one Saturday morning time.

Before saying an appointment was booked, the agent had the caller's agreement: the caller picked one of the times the agent had just offered for that service and day, or said a clear yes to a read-back of it.
By the end of the call the agent had confirmed exactly one appointment, a haircut on Saturday morning.
